# R7 ledger: who decided (generated by `scripts/r7-ledger.ts report`; do not edit)

Rules and definitions: `docs/staging/r7-ledger.md`. Every number below comes from the JSON files of `scripts/r7-ledger.ts receipts`, `scripts/r7-ledger.ts tap` and `scripts/valuation-ledger.ts` (receipts read 2026-10-11 00:13 UTC at 65e0a5c). No model was run and nothing was fitted.

## 1. Today's baseline in four lines

The reference configuration is the first adapter (`r4-rules-state`), gate on, on seeds no adapter was trained on, days 30 to 35 (seeds 21 and 5, 10 focal animals, 5 days, 2707 receipts). The name it may carry: **rules-taught model on a rules menu**.

1. **Kind.** The model picked the kind of act from a real choice for **34.8% to 63.0% of waking minutes** (647 waking minutes per animal and day by the receipts). After each such choice the gate holds the act without asking: counting those held minutes too, 99.9% of waking minutes were in a kind the model had picked. The receipts do not log when the gate took over, so the first figure is a bracket, closed with the run's own counters (the receipts alone give 34.8% to 99.9%). Over the whole 24 hours those counters give 58.3% under a fresh choice, 41.5% under an intention the gate held and 0.2% under the rules.
2. **Target.** It picked the target of **7.6% of acts** (114 of 1494; 10.5% of the 1085 acts that have a target). The rest: 967 acts whose one target was fixed before it saw the menu (the slot cap and the rules' score), 409 acts with no target, 4 set by the rules.
3. **Ending.** No ending was its own: no kernel is asked how long to act or when to stop, and the loop set the moment of every ask. At most **46.4% of endings** (689 of 1484) were its choice to leave an act that was still on offer when the loop asked; 53.2% ended with the act no longer on offer (the body, the world or a cut of the menu), 0.3% by the rules. Asked with its act still on offer, it stayed 63.7% of the time.
4. **Hand-set numbers still read on its path:** the table at the end of this section.

Missing from every receipt, and so from this ledger: why the animal was asked (the trigger); when and how often the gate kept an act or turned a trip into feeding inside an interval; whether an act that left the menu had finished or was cut; how many legal targets stood behind the one on the menu; whether the animal was asleep. Part B measures the first, third and fourth in a rules world; the list of fields a run must log is in `docs/staging/r7-ledger.md`.

Behind the menu itself stand the rules' scores: 94 offer sites over 29 actions, 457 inline score literals, 78 thresholds in the conditions in front of offers, 123 terms switched by who the animal is, and 252 registry parameters (section 5). A rules-taught adapter reads them a second time through its labels.

## 2. Why an animal is asked (shadow tap, a rules world)

The working base on the field map, every animal on the rules, seeds 48 and 7, 30 days of burn-in and 5 tapped days each (seed 48: 49 animals alive at the end, 38 aged 8 and over, 93 s; seed 7: 49 animals alive at the end, 38 aged 8 and over, 92 s). Each world was run a second time with no tap and ended on the same hash.

Decision points read: 46118, of which 12366 (26.8%) by animals under 8, for whom the rules decide and no kernel would be asked. For animals aged 8 and over: 88.8 decision points per animal and day; at 64.0% of them the gate asks again (56.9 asks per animal and day).

### The gate's verdict at each decision point (animals aged 8 and over)

| verdict | class | share of decision points | share of asks |
|---|---|---|---|
| kept by the gate | not asked: the gate kept the act | 29.8% | – |
| an interrupt (a perceived event) | asked: a perceived event | 24.1% | 37.6% |
| the act ended | asked: the act ended | 14.8% | 23.1% |
| a need crossed a threshold (need bucket: 0.4, 0.55, 0.7, 0.88) | asked: a hand-set number | 11.9% | 18.5% |
| arrived: the trip became feeding | not asked: the gate began feeding at the end of a trip | 6.1% | – |
| the 30 minute limit | asked: a hand-set number | 6.1% | 9.4% |
| returning light in the nest (perceived) | asked: a perceived event | 4.4% | 6.8% |
| the clock period changed | asked: a hand-set number | 2.6% | 4.0% |
| the party first holds enough males (perceived; the impulse is a rule) | asked: a perceived event | 0.2% | 0.4% |

**Share of asks by trigger:** a perceived event 44.9%; a hand-set number 32.0%; the act ended 23.1%. This is the rules' own gate on the rules' own acts: a model with the gate on is asked by the same function, about its own acts.

### The trigger at the level of the tick (what made the decision point)

| trigger | all decision points, animals 8 and over | asks only | animals under 8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| the act finished early (the body or the world: arrived, crop gone, sated, partner left) | 22.9% | 26.2% | 17.4% |
| an interrupt (something perceived) | 25.8% | 37.2% | 15.2% |
| the bout's scheduled end (a hand-set bout range, or the walk of a committed trip) | 51.1% | 36.6% | 67.4% |
| the bout was cut short by waking or by returning light (the body) | 0.2% | 0.0% | 0.0% |

With the gate off a kernel is asked at every decision point, so the first column is the trigger mix of its asks; with the gate on, the second.

What the interrupts were (a coarse reading of the animal's own percept line, 8699 interrupts): a call or travel hoo 33.7%; a companion moving off 28.0%; a companion arriving 13.9%; a display, charge or attack 10.8%; grooming begun on it 9.0%; other 3.4%; weather, strangers or other animals 1.2%.

When the verdict was "the act ended" (4995 times), the act held and how it ended: forage: finished 30.6%; pant-grunt: finished 22.2%; travel: finished 10.5%; display: finished 9.4%; charge: finished 4.8%; call: no longer on the legal list 3.4%; submit: no longer on the legal list 3.3%; mate: finished 3.1%; groom: no longer on the legal list 2.5%; flee: finished 1.4%.

So: is a sub-menu needed to choose a tree? A kernel built for 8 options can take the trees of a trip in one question at 0.0% of decision points and needs a wider question or rounds at 100.0%; for trees in view the shares are 100.0% and 0.0%. The whole menu by possibility fits in 8 at 0.0% of decision points. With the fan-out wrapper that exists (`src/kernel/fanout.ts`, rounds of 8) one question over the trees a trip could go to would take 7.8 kernel calls on average keeping the best one of each group and 9.7 keeping the best two; over the animal's whole menu by possibility (without the community's list) 8.0 and 9.8.

## 6. The name each configuration may carry

From the plan's block of 10 October 2026: "rules-taught model on a rules menu" for an adapter taught on the rules' decisions; "untuned model on a rules menu" for the model as shipped; "copy of adapter X, audited, agreement A" for any stand-in; "model-driven" without a qualifier only once the model picks the kind of act, the target and the ending for most of the day and its teacher is not the rules.

"Most of the day" is read here as more than 50% on each of the three lines (this script's reading). The teacher is the adapter's own manifest (`label_source`).
